etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: First attested in 1561, borrowed from Latin relēgātus, the past participle of relēgō (“to dispatch, banish”).
senses: Exile, banish, remove, or send away.
(transitive, in extended use) Consign or assign.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: First attested circa 1550: from the Classical Latin relēgātus (“banished person, exile”), the nominative singular masculine substantive form of relēgātus, the past participle of relēgō (“to dispatch, banish”).
senses: (history, obsolete) A person who has been banished from proximity to Rome for a set time, but without losing his civil rights.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 3
paragraphs: First attested circa 1425: from the Classical Latin relēgātus, the perfect passive participle of relēgō (“I dispatch”, “I banish”).
